lawyer:

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Imman Ali, J:- This Reference under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure made by the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, Third Court, Dhaka is submitted for confirmation of the sentence of death imposed upon accused Shahid Javed Gaira alias Garib Miah, Ismail Mollah alias Galu and Sundar Babu son of Afzal Hossain upon their conviction under Sections 302/34 of the Penal Code by judgment and order dated 18.8.2004 in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 2248 of 2001. By the same judgment five other accused persons were convicted under Sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced to imprisonment for life. 

 3. Subsequent to the admission of the appeals, an application was filed by Md. Kamruzzaman, Advocate praying for drawing up proceedings against the Investigating Officer for including Shah Alam Babu in the charge sheet instead of Sundar Babu, whose name had been mentioned in the First Information Report (FIR). A Suo Motu Rule was issued against the Investigating Officer, Md. Rezaul Karim, being numbered as Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo-Motu Rule) No. 3196 of 2005. Another Suo Motu Rule was issued against the Inspector General of Police and the Metropolitan Police Commissioner, Dhaka, being numbered as Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) No. 3197 of 2005, to show cause as to why they shall not bring into the picture Sundar Babu, son of late Seken Mollah. A further application by the Society for the Enforcement of Human Rights, represented by its Executive Director, Alena Khan, Advocate culminated in the issue of a Suo Motu Rule against the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, being numbered as Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) No. 3198 of 2005. As the Reference and all the appeals arise out of the same judgment and the Suo Motu Rules are connected therewith, they were heard together and are taken up for disposal by this judgment. 

 5. The prosecution case in brief is that at 9.30 p.m. on 14.3.98 the informant, Rokeya Begum found her husband, Gazi Liakat Hossain discussing matters relating to their organization with accused Pichhi Babul, Ismail Mollah Galu, Shahid Javed Gaira, Eunus, Sundar Babu, Shahjahan, Shamim, Shahadat, Mohsin and others in front of No.19 Juriatuli. She told her husband to come home, whereupon her husband was chased to a place in front of the house of one khalek at No. 18 Taherbagh Lane and caught. Accused Pichhi Babul shot at the victim's throat, accused Gaira shot on the left of his neck, accused Shamim shot on his left shoulder, Ismail Mollah alias Galu shot at the victim's chest, Sundar Babu shot at his abdomen and Pichhi Babul shot at his left elbow. The victim then fell in front of the gate of the house of Khalek. The informant rushed and embraced her husband when accused Shahjahan pulled her by the hair and kicked her to the ground. Accused Shahadat, Mohsin. Shamim and Eunus and others created terror by throwing bombs. Upon hue and cry being raised, the accused fled from the scene. The victim was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he died after being admitted there. The informant lodged the F.I.R. with Sutrapur Police Station within four hours of the occurrence. Thus Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 58(3) 98 was started. 

 7. The Prosecution examined 14 witnesses in order to substantiate the case against the accused persons, whereas the defence did not examine any witness. From the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses and the statements given by the accused persons when examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the defence case appears to be one of innocence and false implication. The specific defence case put forward by accused Shah Alam Babu alias Sundar Babu is that he was not the person who committed the offence inasmuch as he was not identified in the dock by the informant or the other witnesses as the person called  Sundar Babu who shot the victim. The specific defence case put forward by accused Ismail Mollah alias Galu and Eunus Mollah is that they have been implicated in the case due to the previous grudge and enmity arising out of dispute over property and pending civil suits. 

 8. The informant, Rokeya Begum, wife of the victim Gazi Liakat Hossain deposing as P.W.1, narrated the prosecution story as detailed above. She witnesses the whole occurrence from the time when her husband was chased by the accused to his being shot by them from close quarters. She identified Eunus Mollah, Ismail Mollah Galu, Shahid Javed Gaira, Shahjahan, Mohsin and others in the dock. In her cross-examination she stated that she now lives at the house of her aunt-in-law at No.12 Juriatuli and at the time of occurrence she lived with her family at 64 Juginagar Lane and that her husband was the General Secretary of the Transport Association and he also owned a sugarcane warehouse. On the date of occurrence, as her - husband was late in returning home, she went to look for him at the house of her aunt-in-law. She stated that she could not recognize all the persons who took her husband to the hospital. She returned home at about 12.00 midnight and after putting the children to bed, went to the Police Station along with her aunt-in-law and others to lodge the F.I.R. She admitted that there was some organizational dispute with her husband and some of the people and that he stood for election as a Member of Parliament in 1991. She also admitted that he had been in jail on account of a false case filed by her husband's adversaries. She denied knowledge of her husband's involvement in the case of bombing of the Prime Minister's Residence and about the shooting of the Police Sergeant as a result of which her husband was allegedly imprisoned for 7½  years. She also denied knowledge of her husband's involvement in the case regarding burning of the bus at Sayadabad in which 50 persons were burnt. She stated that Badsha Mia was her aunt-in-law's son (ফুফাতো দেবর) and that she did not know Jiban, Saidul Islam and Abul Hossain. Monowara Begum is a neighbor of Galu. She admitted that her aunt-in-law filed a separate case against accused Eunus Mollah and eight others, which ended in acquittal. She denied the suggestion that she did not name Eunus Mollah in the FIR. but stated that she could not say whether his name was written there or not. She denied as not true that she did not state in the F.I.R. that Galu, Eunus and others shouted to catch Gazi Liakat; that she ran after the accused persons; that Galu shot at Liakat's chest with a cut rifle; accused Shahadat, Mohsin, Shamim, Eunus and others exploded bombs in order to create terror. She asserted that after the occurrence she caused a separate explosives case to be filed against the accused persons. She denied the suggestion that Pichhi Babul did not shoot at her husband's throat; that accused Gaira did not shoot at her husband's neck; accused Ismail Mollah alias Galu did not shoot at her husband's chest; that the accused were not armed with revolver, gun and cut rifle; that accused Sunda'. Babu did not shoot at Liakat's abdomen and Pichhi Babul did not shoot at his left elbow; and that Shahadat, Shamim, Eunus, Mohsin and others did not explode bombs and, thereafter escape via BCC Road. She stated that she was not a witness or informant with regard to the case concerning the death of Pichhi Babul and she did not know who the informant was, or who was witness in that case. She denied the suggestion that the occurrence did not take place in the manner, time and place as deposed by her. She denied the suggestion that her husband was a top terror and that his,, rivals may have murdered him.She denied the suggestion that she has implicated accused Eunus, Gaira and Galu due to personal grudge arising out of property disputes. In her further cross-examination she stated that her residence is 400/500 yards from the place of occurrence and that she went there by rickshaw. She stated that the house of her aunt-in-law is 1/2  km away from her residence and that she reached there and found he husband taking with the accused persons in front of the house at No.19; that after chasing her husband from that place the accused persons caught hold of him in front of No.18 Taherbag Lane, where she witnessed the occurrence from close quarters. She stated further that she embraced her husband while facing him when accused Shahjahan pulled her by her hair and felled her to the ground and they shot her husband from the front. She stated that at that time there might have been some bloodstains on her body, but she did not hand over the slightly bloodstained clothes to the police and she washed them away. She denied the suggestion that she did not at all go to the place of occurrence and that Shajahan did not pull her hair and that she did not get any blood on her clothes, and that is why she did not hand over any clothes to the Police. She stated that after the occurrence she lost her senses frequently and people poured water over her head and as a result the stains were washed away from her clothes. On recall for cross-examination on 25.6.2003 the witness stated that the person standing in the dock by the name Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu is not the accused in her case. 

 9. Ayesha Khatun, deposing as P.W.2, stated that the victim Gazi Liakat Hossain was her nephew and that he came to her house in the evening of 14.3.1998 and stayed there for 1 to 1½  hours and left at about 8/8:30 pm saying that he would be downstairs. At 9 o'clock she came down and found Liakat surrounded by a number of people, including Gaira, Sundar Babu, Montu, Shahjahan, Shamim, Shahadat and others and a little distance away she saw Galu, Eunus and Pichhi Babul whispering to each other, but she did not suspect anything at that time. On her way back to her residence she saw Galu with a heavy sack entering house No.11. After 15/20 minutes she heard the shouts, "catch him, catch him" (“ধর ধর”) She came downstairs and saw 2 or 3 persons running to the South and Liakat was no longer there. In front of the house at No. 19 she found the wife of Imman Ali, who, upon her query, told her that Pichhi Babul, Galu, Gaira, Montu, Shamim, Shahjahan, Shahadat, Eunus Mollah and others had chased Liakat at gun-point. Then she saw those persons running towards Taherbag and noticed that Eunus, Shamim and lqbal were exploding bombs. When she approached a little further she saw Eunus Mollah and his brother-in-law Joynal holding the collar of the shirt of her nephew (sister's son) Badsha, who along the victim's wife, Rokeya were running ahead of her. When she reached that place accused Eunus Mollah shouted to grab hold of Liakat's aunt (the witness) Liakat as far as the front of No.18 Taherbag and fell down in front of the house of Khalek When the accused persons shouted to grab her (the witness), she quickly ran to the roof of house No. 45 and from there saw Pichhi Babul with his foot on Liakat's chest shooting at his throat; accused Galu shot at Liakat's chest; accused Sundar Babu shot at his abdomen and Shamim shot on his left neck. Accused Montu shot Liakat on his left shoulder and Pichhi Babul shot Liakat on his knee and accused Gaira also shot Liakat. Liakat's wife embraced him before the shooting, when Shahjahan pulled her to the ground by her hair. Afterwards they shot blanks and left the place of occurrence towards the North. The witness and other came to the place of occurrence and took the injured in a van as far as Gulistan and from there in a baby-taxi to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where he was declared dead by the duty doctor. The witness identified accused Galu, Eunus, Shahajahan and Gaira in court and stated that accused Shamim, Sundar Babu, Montu and Shahadat were not present in the Court. She corroborated the statement of the P.W.1 with regard to the vocation and profession of the victim and also stated that she did not hear of her nephew being involved in any antisocial activities. She denied the existence of cases against her nephew. She admitted that she had filed a separate case against the accused persons for exploding bombs in front of her house, which ended in acquittal of the accused. She stated that 5 minutes before the accused chased the victim the electricity failed but there was electricity at Taherbag. She denied the suggestion that she did not tell the Daroga that Eunus said to grab Liakat's aunt; that Eunus and his brother-in-law Joynal caught hold of Badsha's collar. She stated that she went on to the roof of house No.45 belonging to Harun Miah and between that house and the house of Khalek there is a road. She also stated that Liakat's wife grabbed hold of him moments before he was shot and did not hold him after he was shot, when he was bleeding. She denied the suggestion that she did not observe the occurrence from the roof of the neighbouring house and that she was not at all present at the place of occurrence. She stated in her further cross-examination that between No.18 and No.45 Taherbag there is no other investigating house. In cross-examination on behalf of Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain, the witness stated that the person standing in the dock as accused Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain is not the Sundar Babu who is accused in their case. 

 10. P.W.3, Md. Badsha stated in his examination-in-chief that he has a pan and cigarette shop south of Taherbag and that he heard hue and cry at 9/9:30 on 14.3.1998 and thereafter, heard the sound of gun shots. He then saw Liakat running into Taherbag chased by Pichhi Babul; who was shooting, and behind him was Galu, also firing from his gun. They were accompanied by Eunus, Shahjahan, Sunndar Babu and Gaira. He could not recognize the others. Behind the accused persons where the informant Rokeya and Liakat's aunt. He also ran after them and was confronted by Eunus in front of house No. 45. Eunus told him and Liakat's aunt that if they went any further they would be killed. He then went to the roof of house No. 45 and saw Liakat of the ground embraced by his wife. Thereafter, accused Shahjahan pulled her away by her hair and accused Galu shot Liakat in the chest, Pichhi Babul shot him in his throat, Shamim shot at Liakat's head, Sundar Babu shot at Liakat's abdomen and thereafter Eunus and others indiscriminately shot Liakat and left towards the North. Getting down from the roof, the witnesses found the victim bleeding and took him on a van to Gulistan and thereafter by baby-taxi to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where the doctor declared him dead. Police came to the place of occurrence at 4/4:30 a.m. and recovered 2 empty bullet-shells by a seizure list which the witness signed. He identified his signature on the seizure list as Ext. 3/1. The witness identified accused Eunus, Gaira, Shahajahan and Galu in the dock. In his cross-examination he stated that he left a young lad guarding his shop while he ran after the accused persons. He stated that he gave statement to the police on 14.4.1998. In his further cross-examination he admitted that victim Liakat was his maternal cousin. In his cross-examination on behalf of the Sundar Babu, he stated that the Sundar Babu who is accused in the case, was not present in the Court and that the Sundar Babu present in Court was not the actual Sundar Babu who is accused in the case; he is a different person. 

 11. P.W.4, Rehena, is not an eye witness of the occurrence of shooting, but deposed to the effect that she saw the victim in the company of Galu, pichhi Babul, Eunus, Gaira and Liakat's wife in front of house No.19 Juriatuli and then saw Liakat running, being chased by Galu, Pichhi Babul and others who were shooting from their pistols. She also stated that she told Liakat's aunt that she had seen the accused chasing Liakat holding guns in their hands. She heard half an hour later that Liakat had been killed at Taherbag. In her cross-examination, she stated that Eunus Mollah as plaintiff, had filed a Civil Suit No. 230 of 2002 against her. She stated that a false case had been field against her husband because she was a witnesses in this case and denied having received any money as payment for sale of land. 

 22. The accused persons present in the dock were examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. None, apart from accused Ismail Mollah alias Galu, choose to make any statement. It appears that a written statement was submitted on behalf of accused Ismail Mollah alias Galu and Md. Eunus Mollah annexing by firisti papers relating to several cases in an attempt to show previous dispute and enmity between them and the informant party. 

 24. Ms. Fahima Nasrin learned Deputy Attorney General appearing along with Mr. Md. Jamil Akhter Elahi, learned Assistant Attorney General, on behalf of the State submits in support of confirmation of the reference and prays that the appeals be dismissed. She submits that P.Ws. 1.2,3 and 5 were eye witnesses of the whole occurrence and P.W.4 was also an eye, witness of the first part of the occurrence. when the accused were chasing the victim holding guns in their hands, and the prosecution story has been fully corroborated by all the witnesses. She points out from the evidence of the witnesses, that P.W.1 the wife of the victim, was present throughout and saw the occurrence from the very beginning when her husband was being chased by the accused persons and she gave details of how each one of the accused persons shot at the various parts of the victim's body. She points out that the evidence given by the informant at the time of the trials is consistent with the F.I.R., which was lodged by her within 4 hours of the occurrence. She points out that the allegation that Shahjahan pulled the informant by her hair and felled her to the ground is consistently stated by the witnesses. She further points out the evidence of P.Ws.2 and 3, who observes i5 whole occurrence from the roof of house No.45 in Taherbag, is believable as they have stated that there was no obstruction to their view from that place to the place of occurrence. She submits that the question whether the informant embraced her husband before he was shot or afterwards is not so material when the fact remains that the victim was shot at close range and all the eye witnesses have corroborated the fact that the informant was pulled away by accused Shahjahan by her hair and thrown to the ground. She further points out that although P.W.4 was not an eyewitness of the occurrence of the shooting she saw the victim being chased by the accused persons, which was a prelude to the occurrence and supports the prosecution case. She then -points out that P.W.5 is an independent local witness, who saw the occurrence from the beginning to the end and he was examined by the Police within 2/3 days of the occurrence and the defence has not been able to discredit his evidence in any way. So far as the involvement of accused Eunus is concerned, the learned D.A.G. submits that according to P.W.2 he held Badsha (P.W.3) and also told P.W.3 that if they went any further they would be killed. P.W.3 also stated that Eunus and others fired shots indiscriminately. She submits, therefore, that the time place and manner of occurrence have been fully corroborated by the eyewitnesses to the occurrence and the injuries have been supported by the doctor. P.W.7. She submits that the State seeks confirmation of the death sentence in respect of all 3 remaining condemned prisoners. With regard to condemned prisoner Sundar Babu, the learned D.A.G. submits that in the alternative, if the Court is satisfied that Shah Alam Babu, who was present in the dock and not identified as the perpetrator of the injuries, is a different person, then the Court may direct the trial of Sundar Babu, who has clearly been mentioned in the F.I.R. and his involvement has been supported by all the eyewitnesses. 

 25. Mr. S.M. Rezaul Karim, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant who has filed the appeal in the name Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam BAbu, submits that it is abundantly clearly from the evidence of P.Ws.1, 2 and 3 that the person standing in the dock during the trial by the name of Shah Alain Babu, who had appeared in the name Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain, was not the person who was the perpetrator of the crime alleged by the informant and the witnesses. He submits that Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain appeared before the trial Court on 25.6.2003, but the charge as framed by the Court earlier was not read over to him as required under Section 265D(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as a result he has been prejudiced. He points out that Sundar Babu, son of Afzal Hossain was named in the charge sheet, but there is no evidence on record to show how the father's name and address was traced since his father's name and address had not been mentioned in the F.I.R. nor stated by any of the witnesses in their statements recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further points out that on the date when P.W.5 deposed in Court (4.10.2003) the appellant was present in the dock and yet P.W.5 identified in the dock 4 named accused persons excluding Sundar Babu and also stated that the other accused persons were absconding, thereby he did not identify the person standing in the dock under the name of Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu as an accused person. The learned advocate submits that none of the witnesses having identified the appellant as the accused in the case, he is liable to be acquitted. He further submits that the learned trial Judge should be taken to task for having convicted a person against whom there is no evidence whatsoever. He points out that the learned trial Judge has not given any explanation as to why he disbelieved the witnesses who stated categorically that the accused standing in the dock was not the Sundar Babu, who is the perpetrator of the crime. By reference to the decision in the case of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman @ Razibulla vs State, 58 DLR 393, he submits that this Court, being obliged under the Constitution to supervise the lower judiciary, should take punitive action against the learned trial Judge for having convicted a person against whom there was no iota of evidence. 

 26. Mr. Khalilur Rahman Bhuiyan, learned advocate appearing as State Defence Counsel on behalf of condemned prisoner Shahid Javed Gaira alias Garib Miah, submits that there is no consistency among the witnesses as to which part of the victim's body the condemned prisoner shot. He points out that P.W.1 stated that this appellant shot at the left neck, whereas the P.W.2 did not specify the part of the body where he shot and P.W.3 did not attribute any shooting to this appellant and P.Ws.4 and 5 also did not mention that the condemned prisoner/appellant shot at the victim. He submits that in view of such evidence the benefit of the doubt should go to the condemned prisoner since no other witness, apart from P.W.1, mentioned the specific shooting by the appellant at the neck of the victim. He refers to the decision in the case of Nurul Islam and others Vs. The State, 43 DLR(AD) 6 and submits that when there is contradiction and difference in the evidence of eyewitnesses, then that creates a doubt and the benefit of the doubt should go in favour of the accused. 

 27. Mr. Md. Mozammel Haque Mehedi, learned advocate appearing with Mr. Md. Eunus Ali Akond advocate on behalf of appellant Md. Eunus Mollah submits that the name of the appellant does not find place in the F.I.R. and, therefore, his inclusion subsequently by P.W.1 is an embellishment. He then points out that, although P.W.3 mentioned indiscriminate shooting by this appellant and others, this is not supported by any other prosecution witness. Mr Md. Eunus Ali Akond submitted that the appellant was implicated in this case due to grudge and enmity, since there was dispute over property from 1995. He further points out that P.W.1 knew the appellant Eunus Mollah, who was a neighbour of P.W.2, but did not mention his name in the F.I.R. He further submits that there is no overt act attributed to the appellant in causing the injuries to the deceased. He submits that in the absence of any overt act with regard to the killing of the victim, the principle of common intention cannot be applied in the case of this appellant. In this regard he refers to the decision in the case of Amar Kumer Thakur & ors V. The State, 8 BLD (AD)101. He also refers to the decision in the case of Belal Ahmed Vs. The State, 40 DLR 154 and submits that it is essential to prove that he had the intention to commit the offence of murder. In this case, he submits, there is no evidence of any conspiracy or pre-plan attributed to the appellant and therefore, his conviction under Section 302/34 cannot be sustained: 

 29. As mentioned earlier, 3 Suo Mow Rules were issued after the admission of the appeals. None has appeared in support of the Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) Nos. 3196 of 2005 and 3197 of 2005, which were issued upon an application for drawing up proceedings against the Investigating Officer. On the other hand Mr. A.K.M. Zahurul Huq with Mr. Syed Haider Ali, learned advocates appeared on behalf of the Investigating Officer, Md. Rezaul Karim. In Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Moto Rule) No.3198 of 2005 Ms. Sigma huda, learned advocate appears on behalf of the Bangladesh Society for the Enforcement of Human Rights (BSEHR) and submits that the Society, upon investigation through their concerned Officers, found that Shah Alam Babu had been wrongly implicated in the case and convicted in spite of the fact that there was no evidence against him. She submits that the person present in the dock was Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain, whereas thewitnesses deposed in Court that the person present in the dock was not the Sundar Babu, who was the accused in their case. She therefore submits that the wrong man has been convicted and is languishing in a condemned cell having been sentenced to death. 

 30. Learned advocate Mr. Syed Haider Ali, appearing with A.K.M. Zahurul Huq learned advocate, took us through the reply filed by the Investigating Officer. Md. Rezaul Karim, in response to the Suo Motu Rule issued by this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) No. 3196 of 2005. At the very outset the learned advocate submits that the Suo Motu Rule is not maintainable, since the applicable under Section 561A was filed when other remedy was available and since Section 561A o the Code of Criminal Procedure can be invoked only when no other remedies are available. The learned advocate submits that the Investigating Officer submitted the charge sheet upon scrutiny of the memo of evidence and other information disclosed in the Case Diary, which had been collected by his predecessors. He submits that the charge sheet shows the accused to be one Sundar Babu, son of Afzal Hossain of 57 Noya Paltan Lane, Lalbag Police Station and proclamation and attachment was sent to this address under Section 88 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the particulars of the accused were found to be correct. He submitted that the Police Regulation of Bangladesh (PRB) Regulation 263 gives a privilege to the Investigating Officer not to disclose the source of his information and it is sufficient that in this case the name and address of the accused was duly found to be correct upon service of proclamation and attachment upon the accused. He further submitted that the Case Diary shows that the previous I.O. Md. Azizur Rahman (P.W.9) went to the house of the father-in-law of the accused and found present Sundar Bibi (his mother-in-law), which also confirmed the identity of the accused person. Learned advocate further points out that the matter of the identity of the accused Sundar Babu was not raised at the earliest point in time when the informant filed a naraji petition against inclusion of accused Sujan. At that time the informant could have challenged the inclusion of Sundar Babu, son of Afzal Hossain. He further points out that the accused in the dock was examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and raised no objection with regard to his identity and did not say anything in his defence and, therefore, the objection subsequently raised is an afterthought. He also points out that there are at lease 8 pending cases in the name of shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain, which together gave a clear picture in the mind of the Investigating Officer with regard to the identity of accused Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu. 

 31. In this connection we may also refer to the submissions of Mr. S.M. Rezaul Karim to the effect that Sundar Babu, son of Seken Mollah is accused in Kotwali P.S. Case No. 23 dated 9.8.2002 which is pending trial in Sessions Case No. 101 of 2004 before the 2nd Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka. He points out that in the P.C.P.R. column of the charge sheet in that case it is mentioned that Sundar Babu is accused in Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 58(3)98 i.e. the case before us. He further submits that it is highly improbably that the inclusion of Shah Alam Babu by the Investigating Officer was at all based on any information, since it is seen from the statements of the witnesses recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as annexed by the Investigation Officer to his explanation, that only the name of Sundar Babu is mentioned and no mention whatsoever is made either of the father's name or of the address of Sundar Babu. He submits that there is no evidence on record to show any connection between Sundar Babu and Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu son of Afzal Hossain, which could lead to the inclusion of the appellant in the charge sheet. 

 36. In view of the letter from the Jail authorities, mentioned above, we are satisfied that Ismail Hossain Galu died in custody and the case against him is, therefore, abated. Pichhi Babul died before the commencement of the trial. It is also apparent that the presence of accused Shahjahan was corroborated by the eye witnesses and the fact that he pulled the informant away from the victim by her hair and felled her to the ground is corroborated by the evidence of P.Ws. 1, 2, 3 and 5. 

 37. With regard to accused Eunus Mollah we note that although P.W.1 mentioned his name in her deposition, she did not name him in the F.I.R. P.W.2 mentioned his presence as one of those who was whispering with Galu and Pichi Babul and also later shouted to grab hold of her (meaning P.W.2) P.W.3 mentioned the presence of Eunus Mollah in the company of the other accused persons and that he and P.W.2 were confronted by Eunus Mollah in front of house No.45. But there is no specific overt act attributed to him apart from the allegation by P.W.3 that all the accused persons, including Eunus, shot at Liakat indiscriminately. However, we do not find corroboration of the fact that Eunus Mollah along with others shot the victim indiscriminately. P.W.5 simply stated that Eunus Mollah told everyone to leave quickly. This also is not corroborated by any other witness. Thus, although we find the mention of accused Eunus Mollah being present, we do not find any allegation of any overt act vis-à-vis the shooting and murdering of the victim. We are mindful of the decision in the case of Belal Ahmed Vs. The State cited above and particularly, in view of the fact that the informant did not mention him in the FIR though it is a. close neighbor and previously known to her. We also note that PW5, whose statement was recorded by a Magistrate under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, did not mention Eunus Mollah as being involved. We feel that the benefit of doubt should go in favour of the accused. 

 38. With regard to the Shah Alam Babu who appeared before the trial court and having been convicted, filed the appeal under the name of Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu, we find that the evidence is manifestly against his being involved in the incidence, in particular since the informant and the other eyewitnesses categorically stated that the person standing in the dock was not the person accused by them in the case. P.W.5, who is an independent and uninterested eyewitness, did not identify him in the dock although he was very much present at the time when PW5 deposed in Court. We find no other evidence or material to connect the person standing in the dock, who made his appearance in the name Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu, with the murder of Gazi Liakat Hossain. As such we are left with no other alternative but to find that the person standing in the dock, who faced the trial as Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu and was convicted as Sundar Babu, is not the person who was accused by the informant and hence he is to be relieved of the charges levelled against him. 

 39. However, it is gleaned from the correspondence received from the Senior Jail Superintendent, Dhaka Central Jail, Dhaka in his Memo No. ১২১৩০/ভঃশাঃ dated 24.08.06 that Sundar Babu son of Seken Mollah is a different person who was in custody at Dhaka Central Jail from 17.2.2005 till his release on bail on 14.03.2006 and that he was in custody in connection with Demra P.S. CAse No. 50(9)04, Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 19(10)04. Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 13(10)04 and Kotowali P.S. Case No. 23(8)02. Thus we are certain that the person standing in the dock assuming the name of Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu son of Afzal Hossain is distinct and different from Sundar Babu, son of Seken Mollah. We note from the charge sheet in Kotwali P.S Case No. 23(8)02, wherein Sundal. Babu, son of Seken Mollah is an accused that the PCPR records that the same accused in Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 58(3)98 which is the case before us. Therefore, we are left in no doubt that the said Sundar Babu, son of Seken Mollah is indeed the accused person who has been implicated in the instant case and should therefore face trial for this case. 

 43. We have heard the submissions of Mr. Syed Haider Ali at length in support of the Investigating officer. However, he could not satisfy us that the Investigating Officer, Md. Rezaul Karim, had before him any information or materials with which to connect Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal of 57 Noya Paltan, Police Station Lalbag with the , occurrence in question. It transpires from his cross-examination as P.W.14, where he deposed as one of the Investigating Officers, that he did not record any statement of any witness under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he merely relied upon the materials collected by his predecessors. The statements recorded by his predecessors were annexed with his reply filed in Court. We do not find anywhere any information indicating that Sundar Babu was identified as the son of Afzal or that he lived at 57 Noya Poltan, Police Station Lalbag. Thus, to say that the previous I.O. visited the house of the father-in-law of the accused and spoke to his mother-in-law is a fallacious argument. Equally, to say that the Proclamation and Attachment were properly served at that address is, so to say, 'putting the cart before the horse'. Only after the identity of the accused is firmly established can there be any question of locating his house or that of his in-laws. Also to argue that the same accused is named in 8 other cases and, therefore, 'fits the bill' as accused in this case, is a non-sequitur. That is a ludicrous argument. Being named as accused in several other cases does not ipso facto indicate his complicity in his case. Moreover, we note that those cases referred to by the deponent in his reply, do not find place in the PCPR of accused Aundar Babu in the charge sheet of the instant case. The arguments put forward arc attempts at post fact justification and do not explain the ground for inclusion of Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal. The earlier cases in respect of Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal, now mentioned in the reply, were obviously not before the I.O. who submitted the charge sheet otherwise he would have referred to them in the PCPR. It is a mystery as to what prompted the I.O. to include in the charge sheet, as accused, someone by the name Sundar Babu, who is identified therein as son of Afzal of 57 Naya Paltan. Lalbag, when no one mentioned the identifying facts, namely the father's name and address. 

 44. Another argument was put forward that the accused did not tender any reply nor challenged his identity when he was examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Again this is post fact justification and does not explain the inclusion in the charge sheet. Moreover, we note that since the witnesses did not implicate the person (Sundar Babu) standing in the dock, he had no duty to reply. Hence, we do not find substance in any of the submissions made on behalf of Inspector Md. Rezaul Karim. We feel constrained to recommended that action should be taken against Md. Rezaul Karim, inspector of Police, who was one of the Investigating officers in this case and submitted the Police Report including in the charge sheet Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal without any basis whatsoever as a result of which an innocent man has suffered incarceration in the condemned cell. Regrettably, our criminal justice system is not geared to recompense for the loss suffered by this unfortunate person and for that reason we feel that stern action be taken against the Investigating Officer, Md. Rezaul Karim. In such view of the matter Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) No. 3196 of 2005 is made absolute. 

 45. In view of the fact that, we have found that Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal Hossain, who assumed the name Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu during the trial and appeal is not the same Sundar Babu who was accused in the case, we need say no further with regard to the Suo Motu Rule numbered as Criminal miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) 3198 of 2005. Accordingly, Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) 3198 of 2005 is disposed of. 

 46. Having discovered the link between Kotwali P.S. Case No. 23(8)02, wherein Sundar Babu, son of Seken Mollah is an accused, and that the PCPR in that charge sheet records that the same accused is accused in Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 58(3)98, which is the case before us, we feel justified in directing the Inspector General of Police and Metropolitan Police Commissioner, Dhaka to take steps for trial of Sundar Babu, son of Seken Mollah in connection with the instant case, i.e. Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 58 (3)98. Accordingly Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo Motu Rule) 3197 of 2005 is made absolute. 

 47. Before parting with this matter, we observe with much consternation the judgment and order of the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in passing an order of conviction and sentence against the 'Sundar Babu' who was in the dock. The evidence and materials on record quite clearly shows that the person standing in the dock assuming the name Sundar Babu alias Shah Alam Babu, son of Afzal was not the perpetrator of the crime alleged against Sundar Babu, By no stretch of the imagination could that person be convicted and sentenced to death, since we find that there is absolutely no evidence against him. The learned judge observed, with reference to the evidence of the witnesses concerning Sundar Babu that their testimony was not believable and on scrutiny was found to be motivated. He noted that the same witnesses had implicated Sundar Babu in their statements recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that after the charge sheet was submitted giving the name and address of Sundar Babu, the informant did not file any application for re-investigation. We do not find any contradiction in the testimony of the witnesses since they are not denying that Sundar Babu is their accused, but categorically stating that the man in the dock is not that Sundar Babu. With regard to the application for reinvestigation, we find that the reasoning given by the learned Judge to be somewhat shallow. If the informant had known the father's name and address of Sundar Babu then she would have stated so in the F.I.R. In the absence of the accused from the dock, she would be in no better position to realize that the Sundar Babu implicated by IO. is not the one mentioned by her. Moreover, having disbelieved the witnesses who deposed in Court, the learned Judge could only convict the Sundar Babu in the dock if there was some evidence on record to indicate his involvement in the occurrence. The learned Judge concluded that upon overall scrutiny he 'surmised' (sarbik porjaluchonay anumita) that the Sundar Babu in Court was the Sundar Babu involved in the case. Such a conclusion lacks basis fundamental knowledge of criminal justice. An accused cannot be convicted on surmise. There must be direct or very strong circumstantial evidence to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. We are of the view that in passing death sentence upon an accused against whom there is no iota evidence or materials before him, the learned Judge has adequately demonstrated that he is not capable of exercising judicial function. In such view of the matter, in the greater interest of the credibility of our judicial system, we would strongly recommend that appropriate action should be taken to immediately remove Mr. Shamshul Alam Khan, the then Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka from service in any judicial capacity. We also recommend that inquiries be made regarding his efficiency and integrity. 

 49. Criminal Appeal No. 3711 of 2004 filed appellant Shahjahan is dismissed and his conviction and sentence is upheld. Criminal Appeal No. 3316 of 2004 filed by Md. Eunus Mollah is allowed. Appellant Md. Eunus Mollah is acquitted of the charges levelled against him is directed to be released forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
